sections.html:
South of Beaverton and north of Tualatin, Tigard is a Washington County city inside the Portland metro area. Interstate 5 marks its eastern side, Highway 99W slices through the middle, and Oregon Route 217 dead-ends into I-5 within city limits. Road access is rarely a problem, a point that helps when buyers and appraisers line your house up against others nearby.

The city uses two ZIP codes: 97223 north of McDonald Street and 97224 for the southern half. The 2020 population was 54,539, a jump from 42,249 in 2000. Tualatin Valley Fire and Rescue answers calls.

Between 1970 and 2000 the population rose from 6,499 to 42,249, so many Tigard houses date from the 1970s through the 1990s. Roofs, windows and sewer laterals on houses that old are often original or close to it. Owners here frequently price out repairs before they pick a way to sell.

Read $610,500 as a citywide midpoint. Your own house may land well under it if the roof is worn or if tenants have lived there for years, and that gap pushes some owners toward an as-is sale.

sections.h2: Parts of Tigard that are changing
sections.html:
Planning attention concentrates in three places. If your property is in one, ask the city what the current zoning permits before you choose how to sell.

  • Downtown Main Street. It took shape after the 1910 railroad and still anchors the older part of town.
  • Tigard Triangle. Roughly 550 acres in the northeast corner, framed by Highway 99W, Highway 217 and I-5. Voters approved a tax increment financing district in May 2017, and the council rezoned most of the area to Triangle Mixed-Use. Vacant lots, flooding, congestion and broken sewer lines are on the city's list of obstacles.
  • Washington Square Regional Center. Metro counts it among eight regional centers, extending nearly a mile in each direction from the mall. Updated code took effect May 23, 2024.

sections.h2: Is the address inside city limits?
sections.html: Bull Mountain, the hill country to the west, is unincorporated. Voters approved annexing it in 2004, yet residents there have rejected annexation and the legal fight has dragged on. Permits and code rules depend on whether an address falls inside the city, so verify yours before you plan anything.

Washington County runs its tax year from July 1 to June 30 and takes payment in three pieces, with due dates in November, February and May. Pay everything on the first date and the discount is 3%; pay two-thirds and it is 2%. Value appeals must be filed by December 31.

Tax becomes a lien on July 1. A late payment draws interest of 1.333% per month. If ownership changes after July 1, the fall statement may not show the new owner, so ask the tax collector to confirm the figure. Back taxes are a common reason owners look for a quicker sale.

On a sale, quitclaim, contract for sale or any other title transfer, Washington County levies $1 per $1,000 of price. Buyer and seller share liability, so settle in the contract who covers it. Pay, or file an exemption, within 15 days after recording, or a late penalty applies.

Exemptions on the county's list:

  • deeds in lieu of foreclosure and court-ordered transfers
  • a trustee's deed from foreclosure
  • gifts, devises and inheritances
  • transfers between spouses under a divorce or separation order

An heir who receives a Tigard house may qualify for an exemption on that transfer, but when the heir later sells, the sale is taxed like any other.

A seller of a one-to-four-unit home owes every buyer who submits a written offer a signed property disclosure statement under ORS 105.465. Five business days after delivery, the buyer can no longer revoke in writing (ORS 105.475). A seller who never hands over the form leaves that right open until closing ends it.

Under ORS 105.470, court-appointed personal representatives and trustees are excluded, along with lenders selling after foreclosure or a deed in lieu. Families selling a parent's house through an estate may qualify, which can mean lighter paperwork.

sections.h2: Selling a Tigard house for cash
sections.html:
Instead of a listing, showings and a buyer's loan approval, a cash sale is a direct purchase of the house as it stands. You describe the property, the buyer looks it over and writes an offer, and if you agree, a Washington County title company opens escrow and takes care of the deed and recording.

The Oregon steps above still apply. Disclosure, the county transfer tax and the tax proration all appear on the closing statement, and the title officer can walk you through each line before signing. To compare fairly, estimate what a listing would net once repairs, agent fees, carrying costs and months on the market are subtracted.

The Tigard-Tualatin School District covers most of the city, but a small northwestern slice is served by the Beaverton School District, so confirm your address with the district. TriMet buses run through Tigard, and the WES commuter train calls at the Tigard Transit Center. Washington Square Transit Center is the second hub.

1. Send the address, condition and your target date.
  2. Receive the written offer and read the terms.
  3. Title company opens escrow and checks for liens and unpaid tax.
  4. Sign, record the deed and receive your proceeds.

Ask for the settlement statement early so the proration and transfer tax lines hold no surprises.

• ID that matches the deed.
  • The newest property tax statement.
  • Lender and loan number for any mortgage payoff.
  • Notes on repairs or code issues you know about.
  • Lease records for a rental.

faqs.q: Is Tigard in Washington County or Clackamas County?
faqs.a: Washington County, which bills the property tax and also collects its own transfer tax on a sale.

faqs.q: What is the Washington County transfer tax rate on a Tigard sale?
faqs.a: One dollar for each $1,000 of price. Who pays is a matter for the contract, and the money or an exemption filing is due within 15 days of recording.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Tigard?
faqs.a: Three times a year: November, February and May. Paying the whole bill by the November date takes 3% off.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Tigard house that has repairs or code problems?
faqs.a: Yes. Known problems go on the disclosure form when one is required, and the buyer gets five business days to revoke. Cash buyers take houses as they are, so repairs need not come first.

faqs.q: Does the Tigard Triangle affect my home sale?
faqs.a: It can. Most of the area became a mixed-use zone in 2017, which may change what a parcel there can be used for. The city planning office can tell you what applies to yours.
